about: What core-hook-npm-response.py expects of the pre hook's first three npm asks (prefix, root, config), of its own readers, of its lifetimes and of its controls. It was written by reading the product source statically at the line ranges each cite names, the ask contract in AGENTS.md, the macOS ps(1) and strftime(3) manuals, and declaring a synthetic fixture's expected results from that reading. No product ask, ps call or control was run to produce it, and no run's output or candidate record was read to produce it. A role is named by the request the expectation declares (argv template and working directory) and by the source's call slot, never from a claim number, a completion order or a value the hook produced. Every fact the collector keeps is observed with its value, absent with its basis, or unavailable with the operation that did not answer; a comparison is a match, a mismatch of two observed values, or incomparable. A code is the judgment's input: code_parts reads its kind, channel and roles, and scenario_rows decides the linkage and intervention rows from them. Placeholders: @W@ the statement's words, @Q@ the quiet flags, @S@ one ask group's scratch directory, @BOX@ @PROJECT@ @HOME@ @STATE@ @TMP@ the sandbox, @SYSTEM@ the system directories on the hook's PATH. A relation candidate covers one group, the initial attempt and its three roles; another group, a follow-up attempt and a declared shared effect are reported apart. Format 5: an exit is read only after the start of the pid's process was read (target_exit), the observer's releases say what they went on, and the driver's bundles are run as attempts that refer to completed prerequisites explicitly; S0 is the first, small bundle that observes those boundaries.

lstart.why: the date-and-time form of the POSIX locale (LC_TIME d_t_fmt), the locale every query sets with LC_ALL=C. It is a declared reading, not a measurement of any host's ps: a start time in another form, or whose weekday is not its date's, is not read, and the line that holds it makes the whole answer unavailable

ps.query: one ps call is one record: purpose, argv (the scope's ps by path, the mode, the purpose's fields, the collector's own pid as sentinel and the targets), locale C, the timeout, start and end times, and the outcome (exit with its status, signal, timeout or exception) with stdout and stderr as they came
ps.read: read_ps reads a record only when every key is there with its type (timeout included), the argv is the one the scope's ps, the purpose's fields, the targets and the sentinel make, ps exited by itself with a status, stderr is empty, every line reads as the fields with a start time in the form above, the sentinel's row is there and no row names a pid nobody asked about. It returns the rows with the query they answer; nothing else reads a row
ps.exit: target_exit reads an exit only for a pid the answer's own query asked about, and only after the start of that pid's process was read for this child: without it, no row, a Z row, another start time and a missing row under an absence basis are all unavailable (attribution). With it: no row is gone only under an absence basis; another start time is another process (pid-reused), before any Z; Z is a zombie; the same start time is alive. The judge reads an exit-poll only through the target it bound to the child, with the pid the child itself recorded, and only when the poll comes after the child's start record. The observer lets the next child of an imposed completion order go only on the exit record of the one before it (after_exit), and a give-up's releases say so (after_give_up). An exit status's value and a pid reused within one second of lstart are not read
ps.scope: a collection's scope is its run id (32 hex digits from the driver), the host by uname, its boot by the start of pid 1 read with this ps, the user id, and the ps executable by path, real path, device, inode, size, modification time and digest, with the mode. The collector reads its own scope; the judge uses the scope the manifest seals and never reads its own machine
ps.absence: a missing row means no process only under the basis host_basis gives for a host fact of exactly the collection's scope, and only for a query of the same ps and mode whose status is the one the fact measured for an answer with a missing pid; otherwise it is unavailable. A collection whose selected host fact does not hold is refused; no collection runs without one

host_fact.measure: the ps-fact process reads its scope, then starts a holder (the fixture above, which ends by itself with its exit when its input closes), sees it alive with its own poll before and after ps is asked for it, closes its input, reaps it within its wait, starts a second holder, asks for the first alone, sees the second alive before and after asking for both, then closes and reaps the second. Each fact is the parent's own event, written once, in this order. Nothing is signalled
host_fact.expect: the thirteen events in the sequence above with increasing times; the parent's polls show each holder alive where the sequence says so; each holder reaped with the fixture's own exit 0; the alive query shows exactly the collector and the first holder, not a zombie, and ran between the two live polls; the gone query started after the first holder was reaped and shows exactly the collector; the mixed query shows exactly the collector and the second holder, not a zombie, between its two live polls; gone and mixed ended with the same status, which becomes the absence status; and the record's scope is exactly the scope it is compared with
host_fact.lifetime: a holder the parent could not reap within its wait stays the parent's: it publishes the original failure first (ps-fact.partial.json), closes and waits within the wait again and keeps that cleanup's errors apart, writes ps-fact.pending.json naming every unreaped holder, waits for each with no bound and no signal, and writes ps-fact.stopped.json only after every holder was reaped (exit 2). A holder that never ends keeps the process waiting, and no record says it was reaped

scenarios.name: P0-natural
scenarios.about: Every child answers and is let go as soon as its output was read; the claim and completion orders are whatever happened, and are recorded.

scenarios.name: P1-permuted
scenarios.about: The observer lets the children claim their record numbers in one order and exit in another, each different from the source's start order.

scenarios.name: P2-permuted
scenarios.about: A second claim order and a second completion order, each different from P1's and from the start order.

scenarios.name: N3a-slot-swap
scenarios.about: Every request, record and child output is the positive's. After all three children wrote and before any was let go, the observer exchanges the prefix and root response files in the hook's scratch directory, so the hook reads each of the two roles from the other's file.

intervention.premise: the six renames the observer makes after all three children wrote and before any was let go: for each channel, the prefix file to a spare name, the root file to the prefix name, the spare to the root name; each recorded once, in that order, in the journal

scenarios.name: N3b-output-swap
scenarios.about: Every request is the positive's and every record names the positive's answer, but the root child writes the config answer's bytes to its own stdout and stderr and the config child writes the root answer's. Each child keeps its own exit status.

npm_fetch.unknown: npm was not asked which registry this install fetches from: no npm install in this command named where it lands

intervention.premise: each emitting child's own written record shows the sha256 of the other answer's stdout and stderr bytes

scenarios.name: N4-follow
scenarios.about: The initial config ask is refused with ENOWORKSPACES, so the hook asks config again in a new group, in the directory the prefix answer named. The follow-up depends on the prefix answer and is outside the initial relation; the hook's fetch facts come from it.

declared.about: Inputs made from a live launch's own records by named edits, judged by the same oracle and read_pending. D0-D9 test what the oracle does with a missing, duplicated, misplaced or unobserved child and a declared shared effect; J3v put writer-shaped and damaged npm_fetch values into a real exchange's pending record. They are synthetic and are no evidence about a real npm, a real ENOWORKSPACES or a real cache. A declared control whose expectation is a result is judged only beside a base launch that made its intervention; one whose expectation is a verdict only beside a base launch that is as its scenario expects.

edits.effect: the root child reads a file the prefix child writes

value.unknown: npm config failed (exit 1: x), so safedeps cannot tell which registry this install fetches from

controls.about: The author's own controls of this change's boundaries, each with literal inputs and literal expectations. readers and adapters run in the check subcommand. copies and sensitivity run from copies of the tree with the exact edits named; check-controls reads what they left with the standard library and the status their parent saw. A control passes only when its copy is this tree with exactly its edits (applied), every reach fact holds (it got to what it injects or removes), and every signature fact is exactly as declared. A control whose reach facts do not hold is not demonstrated and stays not run: no output, an initialization error or an injection never reached is not a detection. None of these is evidence about a real ps failure, a real slot race or a real npm, and none is an independent verification. No sensitivity copy removes the holder parent's lifetime: without it the copy would leave a live holder behind, which this run does not do. Values are compared as JSON values, so false is not 0. S0's flows, their sensitivity flows and the immutability rows are in the control spec of the external driver.

bundles.about: Each bundle is run as attempts: one invocation of the external wrapper (run.sh <bundle> <attempt> [<ref>]) in a staged run, each in its own new directory, started only on its own acceptance. A bundle that needs another is given one explicit reference to a completed attempt of it (same run, or for S1 only, another run with the same inputs, selection, toolchain and environment). No bundle starts the next. S0 is the first small selection that observes the changed boundaries; its success is not a completed S1. A bundle's judgment is its own; no earlier bundle's control is counted in the N1-N5 rows of S4. Counts are planned from the steps, not measured.

S0.about: the contract alone (3), the F1 matrix with the observer and exit_fact adapters and the host scope comparisons (check-s0, 0), S-F1 (1 with its exact failing cases), then the flows in five scratch runs and the final check-controls. The provenance ps count is the scratch wrapper runs'; the S0 attempt's own wrapper adds one

S1.about: the contract alone (3), every literal reader and adapter (0), the check-kind sensitivity copies (each 1 with its exact failing cases), and check-controls. The driver controls that S1 used to carry are S0's flows

S2.about: the ps host fact of this run (a gate: 0 goes on; 3, the fact measured and not holding, stops the bundle with 3; 2 stops it with 2), then the holder-lifetime copy J4h, then check-controls for S2. ps: the scope query and the three host queries of ps-fact, and J4h's scope query. holders: two in ps-fact, one in J4h. A holder that never ends leaves the bundle pending, with no final status

processes.ps: not fixed: one scope query per collection, then a start query per child, a tree query per written child and exit polls whose number depends on timing

S3.about: each observer copy, then a gate of check-controls for that control alone; anything but 0 stops the bundle. Selected launches: J1-acq 1, S-J1-acq 1, J4a 2, S-J4a 2, J4b 2, S-J4b 2; expected to start: 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 1

S4.about: the twelve launches (native and Bash, P0 P1 P2 N3a N3b N4) and the judgment with the declared D and J3v controls. N5 is a separate fresh validator's own reading, not a step here

not_observed: an exit status's value from outside the hook: macOS gives a process's exit status to its parent, and the observer is not the parent of an ask child; the value is the child's own record and the hook's consumption of it
which bytes the hook read: the observer reads the response files while the child is held and the hook's result depends on them, but no read by the hook is traced
the launch order of the three children: the source starts them in one order (the slots above); nothing here observes the start itself
a process's absence without a host fact of the collection's scope: no collection runs without one, and the judge reads the sealed scope's
the start-time form of any host's ps: the form above is declared, not measured; a host that prints another form leaves every answer unavailable

time: whether the order budget, the children's starts, the ps calls, file I/O and a follow-up config fit inside the hook's shared ask deadline is not measured; an order the observer could not impose within its budget is reported not observed. The close budget bounds the observer's ps calls only, not a scan, a release, a file write or a publish

an observer or a holder that never ends: the collector or the holder parent waits for it without a signal, so the final status is not reached and the pending record is what remains; a record that cannot be written is said on stderr and is not there
real npm: every answer comes from the stand-in; a real npm's shared cache, configuration files and ENOWORKSPACES are not exercised

a completed attempt's own wrapper exit: the completion record is the wrapper's record of the driver's status and of the files it closed, written before the wrapper itself returns; the nohup launcher's pid is no evidence of an end
an S1 reused from another run on another host: accepted only with the same staged inputs, selection, Python and declared environment; an equality that was not shown is not assumed
